name: Syndrome with Alpha-Thalassemia as a Major Feature

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Syndrome with Alpha-Thalassemia

criteria.description: Molecular genetic confirmation of alpha-globin gene deletions or mutations
Presence of microcytic hypochromic anemia with hemoglobin H inclusion bodies
Clinical features including pallor, hepatosplenomegaly, and growth retardation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Molecular genetic confirmation of alpha-thalassemia plus at least one major clinical or laboratory criterion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other hemoglobinopathies and iron deficiency anemia.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hemoglobin H inclusion bodies in erythrocytes
searchTerms: red blood cells with inclusion bodies
Hemoglobin H presence in blood cells

pathognomonic.symptomName: Microcytic hypochromic anemia refractory to iron therapy
Alpha-globin gene deletions detected by molecular testing

searchTerms: pale skin from low red blood cells
skin looks lighter due to anemia

common.symptomName: Growth retardation in infancy and early childhood

searchTerms: yellowing of skin from red blood cell breakdown
skin discoloration from blood cell destruction

occasional.symptomName: Bone deformities due to marrow expansion
searchTerms: bone deformities due to increased marrow activity
abnormal bone shape from marrow growth

rare.symptomName: Cardiac complications secondary to chronic anemia
Iron overload due to repeated transfusions
searchTerms: iron overload due to repeated transfusions
blood cell production outside bone marrow
spinal masses from blood cell growth

laboratory: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with low mean corpuscular volume (MCV)
Presence of hemoglobin H inclusion bodies on supravital staining
imaging: Bone marrow expansion visible on X-ray
genetic: Deletion or mutation of alpha-globin genes (HBA1, HBA2) confirmed by PCR or MLPA
other: Elevated serum bilirubin and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)
Iron studies showing normal or elevated ferritin

distinguishingFeatures: Beta-globin gene mutations instead of alpha-globin
Different pattern of anemia and clinical severity
Absence of hemoglobin H inclusion bodies

redFlags: Severe anemia unresponsive to iron therapy
Signs of cardiac failure secondary to chronic anemia
